entries.text: They said the birds refused to sing... And the thermometer fell suddenly, as if god himself had his breath stolen away. No one there dared speak aloud, as much in shame as in sorrow. They uncovered the bodies one by one. The eyes of the dead were closed, as if waiting for permission to open them. Were they still dreaming of ice cream and monkey bars, of birthday cake and no future but the afternoon? Or had their innocence been taken along with their lives, buried in the cold earth so long ago? These fates seemed too cruel, even for god to allow. Or are the tragic young born again when the world's not looking? I wanna believe so badly in a truth beyond our own, hidden and obscured from all but the most sensitive eyes.

entries.text: Arbutus Ray?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yes.
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: Are you the same Arbutus Ray that worked as a nurse... At the dominic savio memorial hospital in 1979?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yes, I'm she.
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: I'd like to ask you about a patient you treated-- a 14-year-old girl.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I remember. Yes. She was such a pretty young girl. You couldn't forget someone like her, or how frightened she was. Scared for her sweet life. The deputy brought her in. She was shaking like a leaf. Wouldn't let anyone touch her but me. Then the strangest thing happened.
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: You had a vision of her... Dead. Like the parents of amber lynn lapierre.
entries.speaker: Harold Piller

entries.text: No one believed me. Honestly, you're the first person who--
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: So you saw her dead?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: That night in her bed. I blinked and it was gone. She was sleeping as sound as could be. I don't know why, but... It made some kind of strange sense.
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: There were men. They came to pick her up late that night. I assumed the one was her father, but he-- he gave me such a chill when he looked at me... When I asked him would he please put out his cigarette.
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: So, they took her?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: They meant to. But when I took them to her room, she was gone. Disappeared out of a locked room. Just vanished.
entries.speaker: Arbutus Ray

entries.text: Harold. You see so much, but you refuse to see him. You refuse to let him go. But you have to let him go now, Harold. He's protected. He's in a better place. They're all in a better place. We both have to let go, Harold.
